text:
IncidentBot: SEV2 detected for customer NovaEdge (private VPC). Sporadic 5xx from NLB egress targets in us-west-2 causing embeddings and inference calls to fail. Alerts: nlb-target-5xx-ratio, natgw-conntrack-high. Paging SRE oncall @Jamie (oncall) @Priya R.

Jamie (oncall): Ack. I'm oncall and taking lead. Adding @Tobias - NetOps and @Elena (Solutions) to coordinate with NovaEdge. Quick impact summary + immediate plan?

Priya R: Customer report: failures to a single downstream vendor IP 198.51.100.23 started ~09:12 UTC. Other egress destinations ok. NLB target group showing intermittent UNHEALTHY spikes, SG logs show DENY on ephemeral ports around same time.

Tobias - NetOps: Looking at target health now. Ran `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arns arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:...` — multiple targets cycling between healthy/unhealthy with TCP resets. Also seeing NAT instance conntrack counts spike around 09:10 -> possible ephemeral port exhaustion.

Elena (Solutions): NovaEdge is on Dedicated pool d8c-priv and tenant is pinned to specific nat instances. Customer SRE on call says they can tolerate a brief cutover to standby for mitigation.

NovaEdge SRE: Confirmed from our side — we can accept a short cutover to alternate egress IP for up to 5 minutes. Please coordinate DNS TTL if you're going to swap any hostnames.

Jamie (oncall): Proposed immediate plan: 1) Drain the suspect nat instance from the NLB target group 2) Shift tenant default route to standby NAT gateway (tenant-specific) 3) Temporarily add SG allow for vendor IP 198.51.100.23 ->443 (to avoid accidental blocks during retries) 4) Lower DNS TTL to 30s in case we need to swap CNAMEs. I'll execute 1 & 3; @Tobias do 2 & watch conntrack metrics; @Elena coordinate with the customer and lower TTL.

Tobias - NetOps: Executing route shift now: `aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abcd1234 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-standby-0a`. Watching CloudWatch: conntrack count trending down after route change.

Jamie (oncall): Removed nat-instance-07 from target group (set to draining). Applied SG rule: allow tcp 443 from 198.51.100.23/32 with description `temp: allow vendor during egress cutover`.

IncidentBot: Note: emergency change recorded. SG modification tagged `emergency` — change review required post-incident.

NovaEdge SRE: Observability: requests returning 200 now, error rate down to baseline. Latency slightly elevated (~200ms extra) but acceptable. Thanks.

Elena (Solutions): Lowered tenant CNAME TTL to 30s. Will hold monitoring for 15 minutes and keep customer updated every 5.

Jamie (oncall): Observing stable targets and 5xx suppressed. Post-incident immediate actions: open follow-up ticket to (a) size NAT capacity for NovaEdge, (b) add conntrack autoscaling + alert, (c) adjust NLB healthcheck thresholds for this tenant. Will remove temporary SG rule after 30 minutes and confirm with customer.

Priya R: I'll file the postmortem and customer-facing incident note. Timeline: incident start 09:12 UTC (thread_ts 4977751111), mitigation steps executed 09:15-09:18 UTC, stable by 09:20 UTC.

Jamie (oncall): Thanks team — keeping channel open for any regressions. :white_check_mark:
